title: Tenant-level residency policies + retention enforcement + evidence export UX
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: Customers in regulated regions have asked for per-tenant controls to ensure requests and stored artifacts remain in allowed geographies, plus deterministic retention policies and automated evidence exports for audits. Current hosted API supports region routing defaults but lacks: 1) policy primitives that tenants can set (e.g., allowed regions, strict vs. preferred), 2) retention TTLs surfaced in Console and enforced at the serving/runtime layer, and 3) scheduled evidence reports (PDF/CSV) that combine routing logs, retention enforcement records, and KMS/audit metadata.

Goal: Deliver a product surface (API + Console UX) that lets tenant admins declare residency policies and retention rules, enforce them in runtime with observable guardrails, and produce automated evidence packages for compliance reviews. Targeting enterprise and mid-market customers with legal/regulatory residency requirements.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Tenant admin can create/update a residency policy via Console and API that declares allowed regions (e.g., eu-west-1, us-west-2) and enforcement mode (strict | preferred).

AC2: Requests to the hosted API include routing metadata; runtime enforces strict residency policies by rejecting/denying requests that would route outside allowed regions and logs a clear audit record.
AC3: Console exposes retention rules at tenant level (default TTL for generated artifacts and embeddings) and those TTLs are enforced by the storage/cleanup pipeline; TTL changes are audited.

AC4: Admin can schedule a monthly evidence export that bundles routing logs, retention deletion events, KMS key IDs, and a human-readable summary; exports are available as signed PDFs/CSV and appear in the tenant's Security > Evidence page.
AC5: UX includes clear warning banners and migration guidance for customers who previously relied on global routing defaults.
AC6: End-to-end tests exist (integration) validating strict policy enforcement, retention deletions, and evidence generation; telemetry metrics and alerts are in place for enforcement failures.
tasks: PM: Draft policy model and tenant-facing language; align with legal on acceptable evidence items
Design: Wireframes for Policies page, Retention modal, and Evidence exports UI; include onboarding flow for enabling strict mode
Eng: Add residency_policy field to tenant API and Console backend (ENG-5473); create enforcement hook in smart router
Eng: Implement TTL enforcement in object store cleanup (ENG-5530) and ensure deletion events are captured for audit
Infra: Ensure region-aware KMS key tagging and include key IDs in evidence bundles
QA: Build integration tests simulating cross-region routing and retention lifecycle
Docs: Create tenant-facing docs, compliance playbook, and migration checklist
Launch: Beta rollout to select customers, collect feedback, iterate before GA
notes: 2026-03-11: Kickoff with legal and security; legal confirmed required evidence items: routing logs, key IDs, deletion timestamps, admin change history.
2026-03-11: Tradeoff discussion: strict mode forces runtime rejects — impacts developer experience for multi-region apps. Proposed opt-in migration with audit-only preview window.
2026-03-12: Design review: prefer a single Policies page with both region allowlist and retention TTL; add a migration assistant that runs compatibility checks and lists impacted request patterns.
Decision: Evidence exports should be verifiable (timestamped, signed) and downloadable; team will use existing signing service used for SLA reports.
